results.name: within_set_lag1_agreement
results.description: Proportion of consecutive trials (same participant, same set, adjacent trial_index) giving the same answer; observed above null means answers within a set block are more sticky/perseverative than the model's independent per-trial responses.

results.name: block_position_slope
results.description: OLS slope of yes on the within-block position (0 = first target shown for that set in that run of trials, scaled to 0-1 within the block), across blocks of >=5 trials; observed above/below null means people grow more liberal/more conservative as they see more targets for the same set, beyond what the target identities imply.
results.code:
# name: block_position_slope
# description: OLS slope of yes on the within-block position (0 = first target shown for that set in that run of trials, scaled to 0-1 within the block), across blocks of >=5 trials; observed above/below null means people grow more liberal/more conservative as they see more targets for the same set, beyond what the target identities imply.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].to_numpy()
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    new = np.ones(len(df), dtype=bool)
    new[1:] = (s[1:] != s[:-1]) | (ti[1:] != ti[:-1] + 1)
    bid = np.cumsum(new)
    g = pd.Series(np.arange(len(df))).groupby(bid)
    pos = g.cumcount().to_numpy().astype(float)
    size = g.transform("size").to_numpy().astype(float)
    m = size >= 5
    x = pos[m] / (size[m] - 1)
    y = r[m]
    if m.sum() < 3 or np.var(x) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.cov(x, y, ddof=0)[0, 1] / np.var(x))

results.name: round_target_contrast
results.description: Among sets containing no multiple of 10, yes rate on non-member targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate on other non-member targets; observed below null means people avoid round numbers that the examples do not license more than the model (above null: a round-number attraction the model lacks).
results.code:
# name: round_target_contrast
# description: Among sets containing no multiple of 10, yes rate on non-member targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate on other non-member targets; observed below null means people avoid round numbers that the examples do not license more than the model (above null: a round-number attraction the model lacks).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    has10 = np.any(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1.0) % 10 == 0, axis=1)
    mem = np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    base = (~has10) & (~mem)
    a = base & (t % 10 == 0); b = base & (t % 10 != 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: recency_nearest_example_contrast
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples and non-member targets, yes rate when the target is closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one minus the rate when it is closer to the first; observed above null means the most recent example pulls generalisation more than the order-blind model allows (below null: primacy).
results.code:
# name: recency_nearest_example_contrast
# description: For sets of >=2 examples and non-member targets, yes rate when the target is closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one minus the rate when it is closer to the first; observed above null means the most recent example pulls generalisation more than the order-blind model allows (below null: primacy).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    k = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    first = ex[:, 0]
    last = ex[np.arange(len(df)), np.maximum(k - 1, 0)]
    mem = np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dl = np.abs(t - last); dfst = np.abs(t - first)
    base = (k >= 2) & (~mem)
    a = base & (dl < dfst); b = base & (dfst < dl)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: small_target_below_range_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets <= 20 that lie below the smallest example (and are not members); observed above null means people have a small-number bias / extend downward toward 1 more than the model, below null means less.

results.name: in_range_width_slope
results.description: Among multi-example sets, OLS slope of yes on example range width (max-min)/100 for non-member targets strictly inside [min,max]; observed more negative than null means people fill wide gaps less than the model's interval hypotheses do (less negative: fill them more).
results.code:
# name: in_range_width_slope
# description: Among multi-example sets, OLS slope of yes on example range width (max-min)/100 for non-member targets strictly inside [min,max]; observed more negative than null means people fill wide gaps less than the model's interval hypotheses do (less negative: fill them more).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    k = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    mem = np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    m = (k >= 2) & (~mem) & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    x = (hi - lo)[m] / 100.0
    y = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)[m]
    if m.sum() < 3 or np.var(x) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.cov(x, y, ddof=0)[0, 1] / np.var(x))

results.name: within_participant_rate_dispersion
results.description: Mean (over the two 2250-row stimulus batches) of the SD of per-participant yes rates, participants found from trial_index resets to 0; observed above null means people differ in overall yes-bias more than the single shared-parameter model produces.
results.code:
# name: within_participant_rate_dispersion
# description: Mean (over the two 2250-row stimulus batches) of the SD of per-participant yes rates, participants found from trial_index resets to 0; observed above null means people differ in overall yes-bias more than the single shared-parameter model produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    pid = np.cumsum(ti == 0)
    n = len(df)
    half = np.arange(n) >= n // 2
    out = []
    for h in (False, True):
        m = half == h
        if m.sum() == 0:
            continue
        rates = pd.Series(r[m]).groupby(pid[m]).mean()
        if len(rates) > 1:
            out.append(float(rates.std(ddof=0)))
    return float(np.mean(out)) if out else 0.0

results.name: near_edge_above_minus_below
results.description: Yes rate for targets 1-10 above the largest example minus yes rate for targets 1-10 below the smallest example (all sets); observed below null means people extend generalisation downward more than upward relative to the model (above null: upward more), i.e. a directional asymmetry the symmetric interval prior lacks.
results.code:
# name: near_edge_above_minus_below
# description: Yes rate for targets 1-10 above the largest example minus yes rate for targets 1-10 below the smallest example (all sets); observed below null means people extend generalisation downward more than upward relative to the model (above null: upward more), i.e. a directional asymmetry the symmetric interval prior lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    a = (t > hi) & (t <= hi + 10)
    b = (t < lo) & (t >= lo - 10)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
